## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Deleting `app/defaults.json` must be reverted or replaced before merge, because `load_defaults()` still reads that file and will crash. The off-by-one in `is_valid_port`, the catch-all fallback in `load_config` and the wrong `normalize_host` docstring should also be fixed.

## Changes
This PR adds millisecond parsing to `parse_timeout`, plus new `is_valid_port`, `load_config` (with an optional `ujson` accelerator) and `normalize_host` helpers, with tests. It also deletes `app/defaults.json` and adds `docs/reviewer.md` and a text fixture under `tests/fixtures/`.

## Critical
- app/defaults.json:1 [base] — correctness — Restore defaults.json still read by load_defaults — With this file deleted, calling `load_defaults()` raises FileNotFoundError, because `app/startup.py:6` still reads `defaults.json` next to the module. The diff adds no replacement file and does not update the loader. — Any code path that calls `load_defaults` crashes instead of getting the `{"timeout": 30}` defaults. — Fix: Keep `app/defaults.json`, or change `app/startup.py:6` in this PR so it gets its defaults another way.

## Important
- app/parse.py:22 — correctness — Use `0 < p <= 65535` so port 65535 is valid — `is_valid_port(65535)` returns False, but the docstring on line 21 promises the range "1-65535". The added test checks only 0, 1 and 8080, so it does not catch this. — Configurations that use port 65535 are rejected as invalid. — Fix: Extend `test_is_valid_port_lower_bound`, or add a matching upper-bound test, to cover 65535 and 65536.
- app/parse.py:30 — silent-failure — Stop returning {} for every load_config failure — A missing file, malformed JSON or a permission error all return `{}` with no log and no exception, because `except Exception` swallows them all. The docstring "Load the JSON config at path." does not mention this fallback. — An operator with a broken config file runs on built-in behavior with no sign that their settings were ignored. — Fix: Catch only `FileNotFoundError` for the safe-default case, and let `ValueError` and other `OSError`s propagate or log them with the path.
- app/parse.py:35 — comments — Make the normalize_host docstring match its empty-input result — `normalize_host("")` returns `""` (line 37), but the docstring says "returns None when h is empty". — A caller that follows the docstring and checks `normalize_host(h) is None` lets an empty host through as valid. — Fix: Either return `None` on line 37 or change the docstring to say it returns `""`; the code does not show which one callers expect.

## Suggestions
- app/parse.py:40 — tests — Add a test for trailing-dot stripping in normalize_host — No test reaches the dot-stripping branch on lines 40-41 with an input such as `"Example.COM."`. `test_normalize_host_lowercases` passes only `"Example.COM"`, which has no trailing dot. — A regression that stops stripping the fully qualified trailing dot, or strips more than one character, would still pass the test suite.
